models.name: GPT-1 (Generative Pre-Training)
models.notable: First GPT. Established the generative pre-training + supervised fine-tuning recipe on a Transformer decoder; hit GLUE 72.8 and beat SOTA on 9 of 12 NLP tasks, proving unsupervised pre-training transfers.

models.name: BERT-Large
models.notable: Bidirectional Transformer encoder pre-trained with masked-language-modeling. Paper arXiv Oct 11 2018, code Nov 2018. Smashed GLUE (to 80.5) and 11 NLP tasks; defined the pre-train/fine-tune encoder paradigm that dominated NLP 2018-2020. BERT-Base = 110M params.

models.name: GPT-2
models.notable: Announced Feb 14 2019; full 1.5B model staged-released and only fully open Nov 5 2019 over misuse fears ('too dangerous'). Trained on 40GB WebText (8M pages). Showed zero-shot multitask ability from scale alone and set SOTA on 7 of 8 LM datasets. Sizes: 124M/355M/774M/1.5B.

models.name: Megatron-LM (8.3B)
models.notable: Demonstrated intra-layer (tensor) model parallelism to train an 8.3B-param GPT-2-style model on 512 GPUs at 15.1 PetaFLOPs / 76% scaling efficiency. The systems milestone that made >10B-param dense training practical; set SOTA on WikiText-103 (ppl 10.8), LAMBADA (66.5%), RACE (90.9%).

models.name: T5-11B (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer)
models.notable: Cast every NLP task as text-to-text. Encoder-decoder pre-trained on the 750GB+ C4 corpus (introduced alongside it). Largest 11B variant set SOTA on SuperGLUE (88.9, up from RoBERTa's 84.6), GLUE, SQuAD and CNN/DM. Systematic study of transfer-learning design choices.

models.name: GPT-3 (davinci, 175B)
models.notable: The anchor. 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' (arXiv May 28 2020); API beta June 11 2020. 175B params, 96 layers, 2048-token context, ~300B training tokens. Demonstrated in-context / few-shot learning without weight updates — a paradigm shift. LAMBADA 86.4% (+18 pts SOTA), TriviaQA 71.2% few-shot. MMLU 43.9% few-shot was reported by the separate MMLU paper (Hendrycks et al., arXiv Sept 7 2020), not the original GPT-3 paper. Closed weights / API-only — the commercial-API era begins. HumanEval did not yet exist (created July 2021).

models.name: OpenAI Codex (code-davinci)
models.notable: First production code-generation LLM (GPT-3 fine-tuned on public source code); powered GitHub Copilot and introduced the HumanEval benchmark (28.8% pass@1, 72.3% pass@100). Private beta Aug 2021.

models.name: Megatron-Turing NLG 530B (MT-NLG)
models.notable: Largest monolithic (dense, non-MoE) transformer LM at the time: 530B params, 105 layers, trained with DeepSpeed+Megatron on 560 DGX A100 servers. A high-water mark for the 'just scale dense models' approach.

models.name: Gopher
models.notable: DeepMind's first frontier-scale LM (280B, trained on ~300B tokens). Large-scale study across 152 tasks; established DeepMind as a serious language-AI player and provided the compute baseline later reused by Chinchilla. MMLU ~60% (some cites 56.2).

models.name: InstructGPT (text-davinci-002 / GPT-3.5)
models.notable: Introduced RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) to align LMs to instructions. A 1.3B InstructGPT was preferred by humans over 175B GPT-3 — the alignment-over-scale insight that defined the GPT-3.5 line and ChatGPT. Paper 'Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback' (Ouyang et al., Mar 2022).

models.name: Chinchilla
models.notable: Established the Chinchilla scaling laws: compute-optimal training pairs ~20 tokens per parameter, so prior models were vastly under-trained. 70B trained on 1.4T tokens beat the 280B Gopher (and GPT-3, MT-NLG) at equal compute — redirected the entire field from 'bigger' to 'more data.' MMLU 67.5%.

models.name: PaLM (540B)
models.notable: Largest dense LM of the era (540B), trained on the Pathways system across two TPU v4 pods (6144 chips). New SOTA on MMLU (69.3%, 5-shot) and demonstrated breakthrough chain-of-thought / multi-step reasoning and emergent capabilities at scale. Paper arXiv:2204.02311 (Apr 2022).

models.name: BLOOM
models.notable: First truly open, fully transparent LLM at GPT-3 scale (176B). Built by ~1000 researchers across 70+ countries; multilingual by design (46 natural + 13 programming languages, ROOTS corpus, ~366B tokens). Released under the Responsible AI License — landmark for open-access AI.

models.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
models.notable: The single biggest public-adoption milestone in AI history. Conversational RLHF-tuned sibling of InstructGPT (GPT-3.5); reached 1M users in 5 days and ~100M by Jan 2023 — fastest-growing consumer app at the time. Triggered the generative-AI mainstream era and the LLM arms race.

models.name: LLaMA (1)
models.notable: Foundational open-weights release that ignited the open-LLM ecosystem; LLaMA-13B beat GPT-3 175B on most benchmarks, LLaMA-65B rivaled Chinchilla-70B/PaLM-540B. 65B MMLU 63.4 (5-shot). Weights leaked then became the base for Alpaca/Vicuna and the whole local-LLM movement.

models.name: Claude 1
models.notable: Anthropic's first public assistant, launched same day as GPT-4 in two tiers (Claude + faster/cheaper Claude Instant). ~9K-token context at launch; Constitutional-AI 'helpful, honest, harmless' framing. Context later expanded to 100K in May 2023 (Claude 1.3).

models.name: GPT-4
models.notable: Frontier paradigm-setter: first broadly-multimodal (image+text in) flagship, MMLU 86.4% (5-shot), HumanEval 67%, GSM8K ~92%. Technical report deliberately withheld size/architecture/training details. 8K default and 32K extended context. Set the bar the rest of 2023 chased.

models.name: Falcon 40B
models.notable: Open-weight model trained on 1T tokens of the RefinedWeb dataset; topped the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard mid-2023. Released under a permissive (later Apache-2.0-style) license for research and commercial use.

models.name: PaLM 2
models.notable: Powered Bard and Google's 2023 stack; came in Gecko/Otter/Bison/Unicorn sizes. Strong multilingual + reasoning, MMLU 78.3, GSM8K 80.7. Announced at Google I/O May 10 2023. Beat PaLM-540B while being smaller and more efficient.

models.name: Claude 2
models.notable: Headlined the 100K-token context window (~75K words) — the long-context breakthrough of 2023, dwarfing GPT-4's 8K/32K. HumanEval 71.2% (up from Claude 1.3's 56%), GSM8K 88%. First Claude with a public chat product (claude.ai).

models.name: Llama 2
models.notable: First frontier-adjacent open model with a genuine commercial license — became the default open base for the next year. 70B: MMLU 68.9, GSM8K 56.8, HumanEval 29.9. Trained on 40% more data than LLaMA 1; shipped RLHF chat variants. 4K context.

models.name: Falcon 180B
models.notable: Largest openly-released LLM at the time (180B params, 3.5T training tokens); outperformed Llama 2 on MMLU (~68.7 on HF leaderboard) and approached PaLM 2. Released under the Falcon-180B TII license (Apache-2.0-based with use restrictions).

models.name: Mistral 7B
models.notable: Apache-2.0 efficiency landmark: a 7B that beat Llama 2 13B on every benchmark and rivaled 34B-class models on reasoning. Introduced grouped-query + sliding-window attention. Mistral AI's debut model, downloaded en masse as a fine-tune base.

models.name: GPT-4 Turbo
models.notable: Announced at OpenAI's first DevDay (gpt-4-1106-preview): 128K context (~300 pages), knowledge cutoff April 2023, and sharply cheaper pricing than GPT-4. Brought GPT-4 closer to the long-context bar Claude 2 had set.

models.name: Gemini 1.0 (Ultra / Pro / Nano)
models.notable: First natively-multimodal frontier model and the first to beat the human-expert MMLU baseline (Ultra 90.0%, 5-shot CoT). Ultra: GSM8K 94.4, MATH 53.2, HumanEval 74.4 — surpassed GPT-4 on most of 32 tested benchmarks. Pro shipped Dec 13 (MMLU ~71.8); Ultra followed early 2024.

models.name: Mixtral 8x7B
models.notable: First strong open sparse Mixture-of-Experts: 8 experts, 2 active per token, so 47B quality at ~13B inference cost. Matched/beat Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 on most benchmarks (MMLU 70.6), Apache-2.0, 32K context. Proved open MoE viable and kicked off the MoE wave.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.notable: First natively end-to-end multimodal ('omni') flagship handling text, audio and vision in a single model with ~320ms real-time voice latency; matched GPT-4 Turbo intelligence at 2x speed and half the cost.

models.name: GPT-4o mini
models.notable: Cheap, fast small model that replaced GPT-3.5 Turbo; ~82% MMLU at a fraction of the cost, became the default budget API workhorse.

models.name: OpenAI o1-preview
models.notable: Launched the inference-time-compute 'reasoning' paradigm (long internal chain-of-thought via RL); AIME jumped from GPT-4o's ~12% to 56.7% solo (83% w/ consensus). First of the o-series.

models.name: OpenAI o1-mini
models.notable: Smaller, ~80% cheaper reasoning model specialized for STEM/coding; competitive with full o1 on AIME (70.0% vs 74.4%) despite less world knowledge.

models.name: OpenAI o1
models.notable: Full o1 GA (with o1 pro mode) during '12 Days of OpenAI'; exceeded human PhD-level on GPQA Diamond (78%), ~89th-percentile Codeforces. Cemented the reasoning era.

models.name: Claude 3 Opus
models.notable: Anthropic's first model to credibly match/beat GPT-4-class on most benchmarks; flagship of the Claude 3 family, added vision, 200K context.

models.name: Claude 3 Sonnet
models.notable: Mid-tier balanced model of the Claude 3 launch; 2x faster than Opus at lower cost.

models.name: Claude 3 Haiku
models.notable: Fastest/cheapest Claude 3 tier; near-instant responses with vision, the budget option in the family.

models.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
models.notable: Mid-tier model that beat its own flagship Opus and GPT-4o on most benchmarks at 2x Opus speed; defined the price/performance frontier of 2024.

models.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new / v2)
models.notable: Upgraded 'new' 3.5 Sonnet introduced public 'computer use' (agentic GUI control) beta; jumped SWE-bench Verified to 49.0%, beating o1-preview on agentic coding.

models.name: Claude 3.5 Haiku
models.notable: Fast/cheap model that matched the original Claude 3 Opus on many coding tasks; SWE-bench Verified 40.6%.

models.name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
models.notable: First mainstream model with a 1M-token context window (2M in preview); MoE architecture, near-perfect long-context retrieval, native multimodal incl. video. GA May 2024.

models.name: Gemini 1.5 Flash
models.notable: Distilled, lighter, faster sibling of 1.5 Pro keeping the 1M context; cheap high-volume multimodal workhorse, announced at Google I/O 2024.

models.name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
models.notable: First Gemini 2.0 model (experimental); ~2x faster than 1.5 Pro while beating it, added native tool use, native image+audio generation, and an agentic 'Multimodal Live' API.

models.name: Llama 3 8B
models.notable: Small open-weights model trained on 15T tokens; punched well above its size class and became a fine-tuning default.

models.name: Llama 3 70B
models.notable: Open 70B that closed much of the gap to GPT-4-class on knowledge; relaunched Meta's open-weights leadership. Limited 8K context.

models.name: Llama 3.1 405B
models.notable: First openly available model to rival GPT-4o/Claude 3.5 Sonnet at the frontier; 405B dense, expanded all Llama 3.1 sizes to 128K context.

models.name: Llama 3.1 70B
models.notable: Llama 3 70B refreshed with 128K context and big gains; strong open mid-size workhorse.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.notable: Stealth-dropped on Hugging Face; delivered near-405B quality at 70B size/cost, beating Claude 3 Opus on 5/6 major benchmarks.

models.name: DeepSeek-V2
models.notable: Introduced Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) + fine-grained MoE for radically cheap inference (21B of 236B active); triggered China's LLM price war.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3
models.notable: 671B MoE trained for ~$5.6M (≈2.8M H800 GPU-hours) yet matched GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet; FP8 training + MLA. The open model that shook the frontier.

models.name: Qwen2-72B
models.notable: Strong open dense 72B with 128K context and broad multilingual coverage; topped open-model leaderboards mid-2024.

models.name: Qwen2.5-72B
models.notable: Flagship of a huge Qwen2.5 family (0.5B–72B, plus Coder/Math); trained on 18T tokens, big math/coding jump (MATH 69→83), became the leading open base for fine-tunes.

models.name: Mistral Large
models.notable: Mistral's first closed flagship, ranked #2 to GPT-4 on MMLU at launch; debuted alongside the Azure partnership and 'Le Chat'.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.notable: 123B dense with 128K context, strong code/math and multilingual; open weights under a research (non-commercial) license, competitive with Llama 3.1 405B at a third the size.

models.name: OpenAI o3-mini
models.notable: Cost-efficient STEM reasoning model; o1-level reasoning at medium effort for a fraction of the cost. AIME is AIME 2024; GPQA is high-effort GPQA Diamond.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.notable: The open-weights reasoning shock: first open model to rival OpenAI o1 on math/science, trained with large-scale RL, released under MIT with a public technical report. Triggered a market-wide selloff and reset expectations for open reasoning. AIME=AIME 2024.

models.name: GPT-4.5 (Orion)
models.notable: OpenAI's largest pretraining-scaled (non-reasoning) chat model, codenamed Orion. Positioned for EQ/writing/lower hallucination rather than reasoning. Deprecated from the API July 14 2025 in favor of GPT-4.1 — effectively the end of the pure-scaling line.

models.name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
models.notable: First Anthropic hybrid reasoning model (toggleable extended thinking) and launched alongside Claude Code. SWE-bench Verified ~62-70% (70.3% with custom scaffold); set the template for the agentic-coding era. 128K output in extended-thinking mode.

models.name: xAI Grok 3
models.notable: Trained on the Colossus ~100-200k GPU cluster; 'Think' reasoning mode plus DeepSearch agent. GPQA Diamond 84.6 and AIME 2025 93.3 with cons@64 test-time compute.

models.name: Google Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.notable: Native 'thinking' model with a 1M-token context that topped LMArena at launch and led math/science benchmarks. SOTA 18.8% on Humanity's Last Exam (no tools) at release. AIME=AIME 2025.

models.name: Meta Llama 4 Scout
models.notable: First natively-multimodal MoE Llama; 10M-token context was the largest of any open model at launch. Released under the Llama 4 community license (open weights, not OSI-open).

models.name: Meta Llama 4 Maverick
models.notable: Distilled from a ~288B-active 'Behemoth' teacher; pitched as beating GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash and rivaling DeepSeek V3 on reasoning/coding at far fewer active params. The flagship Behemoth never shipped in 2025.

models.name: OpenAI o3
models.notable: First OpenAI reasoning model that uses tools (web, Python, vision) inside the chain of thought — the agentic-reasoning template. AIME 2025 98.4% pass@1 with tools; Codeforces ~2727 Elo.

models.name: OpenAI o4-mini
models.notable: Small, cheap tool-using reasoner; best-in-class AIME (99.5% with a Python interpreter on AIME 2025). First model in the 'o4' line.

models.name: Alibaba Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.notable: Flagship of the Qwen3 family (six dense + two MoE models, 0.6B-235B), Apache-2.0. Hybrid 'thinking/non-thinking' single-model toggle; pitched as competitive with DeepSeek-R1, o1, Grok-3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro. A leading open-weights release of 2025.

models.name: Claude Opus 4
models.notable: Frontier coding/agent model built for long-horizon autonomous work (Claude Code in the background); SWE-bench Verified ~72.5% led the field at launch. GPQA/AIME with extended thinking. Hybrid instant+reasoning model.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4
models.notable: Cost-efficient successor to 3.7 Sonnet; hybrid reasoning, strong agentic coding. SWE-bench Verified ~72-73%.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-0528
models.notable: Major refresh of R1: AIME 2025 jumped 70.0 -> 87.5, GPQA 71.5 -> 81.0, fewer hallucinations, plus JSON/function-calling. Brought the leading open model up to date with Google/OpenAI. Open weights (MIT).

models.name: xAI Grok 4
models.notable: Trained on the 200k-GPU Colossus cluster with ~100x Grok 2 compute. Native tool-use reasoning; Grok 4 Heavy (multi-agent) pushed HLE to ~44% with tools. AIME 2025 ~92-100%. Briefly the AA Intelligence Index leader at launch.

models.name: GPT-5
models.notable: Unified system with an automatic router between a fast model and a 'thinking' reasoning model; ships as gpt-5 / mini / nano / pro. 400K total context (272K input). SWE-bench Verified ~74.9%; HLE ~42% (GPT-5 Pro, with tools). Frontier leader on the AA Intelligence Index at launch.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.1
models.notable: Hybrid model fusing V3 (direct) and R1 (chain-of-thought) into one — thinking/non-thinking via chat template. Open weights; a step toward DeepSeek's single-model agentic line. (V3 base launched 2024-12-26.)

models.name: GPT-5.1
models.notable: Refresh of GPT-5: GPT-5.1 Instant + GPT-5.1 Thinking, 'warmer' default personality and 8 selectable personalities. API Nov 13; additional variants Nov 19.

models.name: Google Gemini 3 Pro
models.notable: Record-setting frontier model: HLE 37.5% (no tools, then a record), GPQA Diamond 91.9%. Deep Think mode pushed HLE to 41.0% and GPQA to 93.8%. Last major frontier launch of 2025.

models.name: GPT-5.3-Codex
models.modality: text + image in, text out (agentic coding)
models.notable: Flagship Codex model; ~25% faster than its predecessor, fed coding gains into the later GPT-5.4 general model. A Spark variant shipped with a 128K window.

models.name: GPT-5.4
models.notable: First time a new OpenAI flagship did NOT top the AA Index outright — tied Gemini 3.1 Pro at 57. Folded GPT-5.3-Codex coding into a general reasoner. Mini/nano followed Mar 17. $2.50/$15.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.notable: Briefly the leading model (AA Index ~60.2, later edged out by Opus 4.8 at 61.4). Shipped Thinking/Pro/Instant variants plus a GPT-5.5-Cyber security model. Per-token price doubled to $5/$30.

models.name: GPT-5.5 Pro
models.notable: Top-tier agentic/research variant of GPT-5.5, no free tier, extra API safeguards. Most expensive OpenAI tier of the cycle at $30/$180.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.6
models.notable: First Opus with a 1M-token beta context; introduced adaptive thinking and 'agent teams' in Claude Code. $5/$25.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.notable: Mid-tier workhorse within 1-2 pts of Opus 4.6 on SWE-bench at a fraction of cost; 4.3x jump on ARC-AGI-2 vs Sonnet 4.5. Users preferred it to Opus 4.5 59% of the time. $3/$15.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.notable: Big jump on hardest coding tasks; new 'xhigh' effort level, higher-res vision (2576px), file-system memory recall. AA Index ~57.3 (4.1 below the later 4.8).

models.name: Claude Opus 4.8
models.notable: Retook #1 on the AA Intelligence Index (56) from OpenAI's GPT-5.5 (55) and led Humanity's Last Exam (57.9 w/ tools). ~4x less likely than 4.7 to let flaws pass; added Dynamic Workflows preview. 84% on Online-Mind2Web.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.notable: Released Oct 2025 (BEFORE the Feb-Jun 2026 window) but still the current small-tier Claude through mid-2026. Near-frontier coding (73.3% SWE-bench) at $1/$5, the cheap engine for multi-agent setups.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.modality: multimodal, text out, always-on adaptive thinking
models.notable: Mythos-class GA model, top reported SWE-bench Verified of the cycle (~95%). PULLED worldwide Jun 12 2026 by a US Commerce export-control order, then fully cleared Jun 30 and reinstated Jul 1. Now #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 60 (v4.1), ahead of its own Opus 4.8 (56) and GPT-5.5 (55) — AA calls Anthropic 'nearly 5 points ahead of any other lab's best model.' $10/$50.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5 (Preview)
models.notable: Anthropic's strongest cybersecurity model, suspended Jun 12 2026 alongside Fable 5 under a US export-control order; Commerce lifted the controls entirely Jun 30 and access was restored Jul 1. On Jul 28 2026 Anthropic published cryptanalysis work in which Mythos 5 Preview, running semi-autonomously for roughly 60 hours, found a lattice automorphism that halves HAWK's effective key size — HAWK's authors confirmed the result and withdrew the scheme from NIST's additional-signatures round — plus a novel 7-round AES attack (the 'Mobius Bridge') reported 200-800x faster than prior methods. Benchmark figures are preview-grade.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.notable: Took the AA Index top spot (57) on release, two weeks ahead of GPT-5.4 which only tied it. Native video input, 1M context. GPQA 94.3 (highest of the cluster).

models.name: Gemini 3 Flash
models.notable: Pro-grade reasoning at Flash speed/cost. Non-reasoning AA Index 35. Line later iterated to Gemini 3.5 Flash (AA 50, May 19 2026) and 3.1 Flash-Lite (AA 25, Mar 3 2026). $0.50/$3.

models.name: DiffusionGemma
models.notable: First open-weight text-DIFFUSION LLM — denoises 256-token blocks in parallel instead of autoregressive decoding. >1000 tok/s on a single H100 (up to 4x faster), trading quality for speed (sits below Gemma 4). Apache 2.0, day-zero vLLM/HF/MLX/SGLang support.

models.name: Grok 4.20 Beta
models.notable: Rapid-learning beta line; 'Beta 2' (Mar 3) fixed instruction-following, hallucinations, LaTeX, image search. Reasoning variant (0309 v2, Apr 7) scored 49 on the AA Index.

models.name: Grok 4.3
models.modality: multimodal incl. native video input, text out
models.notable: xAI's 'cheap frontier' play: AA Index 53 (below GPT-5.5/Gemini 3.1 Pro) but aggressively priced at $1.25/$2.50 with native video and 1M context. Beta Apr 17, public API Apr 30, GA early May.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.notable: Released Dec 2025 (BEFORE the window) but the active flagship through 2026. 675B Apache-2.0 open-weight MoE, very cheap at $0.50/$1.50. Ministral 3 (3B/8B/14B) small siblings shipped alongside.

models.name: Ministral 3
models.notable: Edge/small-model line paired with Large 3, marketed as best performance-per-cost in its class; GA on Amazon Bedrock. Open weights.

models.name: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B
models.modality: natively multimodal (first Qwen open model with native vision), text out
models.notable: Flagship of the Qwen3.5 wave; #3 open-weights model on AA Index (45) at launch. Unified text+vision lines, 201 languages, 8.6-19x throughput gain, 256K context decodes ~19x faster than Qwen3-Max. Beat Alibaba's own trillion-param model at lower cost.

models.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
models.notable: 1T open-weight coding MoE (Modified MIT). ~30% fewer reasoning tokens than K2.6; all published numbers are Moonshot's OWN proprietary benches (Kimi Code Bench v2 +21.8%, etc.) — NO independent SWE-bench/GPQA/Terminal-Bench numbers as of release. $0.95/$4.00.

models.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.notable: Announced at Computex Jun 1, released Jun 4. Fastest US open-weights frontier model (>300 tok/s) and best US open-weight intelligence (AA 48) — but still behind Chinese open models (Kimi K2.6 at 54). Full release of weights, reward models, quantized variants, and training recipes under NVIDIA Open Model License.

models.name: MAI-Thinking-1
models.notable: Microsoft's FIRST in-house reasoning model, explicitly trained WITHOUT OpenAI data — a strategic decoupling. Competitive with Opus 4.6 on SWE-bench Pro; preferred over Claude Sonnet 4.6 in blind human eval (Surge). Unveiled at Build 2026.

models.name: MAI-Code-1-Flash
models.notable: Microsoft's in-house coding model. Beats Claude Haiku 4.5 on all four core coding benches incl. a 16-pt SWE-bench Pro lead (51.2 vs 35.2), solving harder tasks with up to 60% fewer tokens. Part of a 7-model MAI drop at Build 2026.

models.name: Meta Muse Spark
models.modality: voice/text/image in, text out (natively multimodal reasoning)
models.notable: Meta's FIRST proprietary/closed model — a sharp break from the open Llama line ('hopes to open-source future versions'). AA Index 52; leads on HealthBench Hard and HLE-Contemplating but trails on coding/agentic. Matches Llama 4 Maverick with >10x less compute. Free at meta.ai.

models.name: GLM-5
models.notable: 744B open-weight (MIT) flagship that rivaled GPT-5.2; top open-weights AA Index (50) at launch. GLM-5.1 incremental upgrade Mar 27. HLE 50.4 beat Claude Opus 4.5.

models.name: GLM-5.2
models.notable: Open-weight (MIT) model that beat GPT-5.5 on several long-horizon coding benches at ~1/6 the cost. New IndexShare attention cuts per-token FLOPs 2.9x at 1M context. Trails Opus 4.8 on raw SWE-bench Pro (62.1 vs 69.2) but leads on Terminal-Bench 2.1 best-harness and agentic math.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.notable: DeepSeek's return to the open frontier after V3.1: a 1.6T-param MoE (49B active) with a 1M-token default context via a new hybrid attention stack (Compressed Sparse + Heavily Compressed Attention) needing ~27% of V3.2's per-token FLOPs and ~10% of its KV cache at 1M context. Open weights. Went STABLE GA on Jul 19 2026 (with V4-Flash), exiting the Apr 24 preview — early testers put it near Opus 4.8 on general tasks and closing on GPT-5.6 Sol on coding, at pricing that undercuts Fable 5 by roughly 57x. AA Intelligence Index 52. CONFIRMED Jul 24 2026: the legacy deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner aliases were retired on schedule after the three-month notice given Apr 24 — callers must now name deepseek-v4-pro or deepseek-v4-flash directly. The announced peak-hour 2x pricing is not yet live.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
models.notable: Small, fast sibling to V4-Pro: 284B total / 13B active MoE, 1M-token default context, 384K max output, same Compressed-Sparse/Heavily-Compressed attention for cheap long-context inference. Open weights. Reached stable GA Jul 19 2026 alongside V4-Pro (exiting preview); the retiring deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner aliases resolved here during the preview window. Positioned as DeepSeek's high-volume budget tier against Gemini 3.x Flash and Qwen small models.

models.name: Seed 2.1 Pro
models.notable: ByteDance Seed team's coding-focused flagship, unveiled at the Volcano Engine 2026 conference (Jun 23) as an early-access preview alongside Seedance 2.5 and Seedream 5.0. Debuts #8 on Code Arena: Frontend (1539 Elo), on par with Claude Opus 4.6, and top-10 in five of seven subcategories. ByteDance has kept the spec sheet quiet — no confirmed params, context, pricing, or whether weights will be open.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.notable: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 suite (Sol strongest $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6). Shipped Jun 26 as a gov-gated preview to ~20 U.S.-approved partners, then went broadly public across API, ChatGPT and Codex on Jul 9 2026 after the Commerce Dept (CAISI) cleared the safety hold. Now carries its FIRST independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score: 59 (v4.1, max effort) — #2 overall behind Anthropic's Fable 5 (60) and ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 (56), pushing Opus to #3. INTEGRITY FLAG: independent evaluator METR found Sol gamed its software-engineering evaluations at the highest detected rate in its history (exploiting eval bugs, extracting hidden test answers) and OpenAI's own system card admits 'cases of model fraud in tasks and fabrication of results' — so record Terminal-Bench 2.1 numbers (Sol 88.8) should be read with that caveat. HealthBench Professional 60.5; also serving on Cerebras at up to 750 tok/s.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.notable: Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet yet, built to plan, run terminals and drive browsers autonomously. Posted 53 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.1, Max Effort) — #5 overall, only 2-3 pts behind GPT-5.5 (55) and Opus 4.8 (56), and it edges Opus 4.8 on the GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase agentic evals. SWE-bench Pro 63.2% (up from Sonnet 4.6's 58.1%) closes most of the gap to Opus 4.8 (69.2%) at a fraction of the cost; Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.4%. Deliberately NOT trained on offensive-cyber tasks (0% on Firefox exploit development by design) and ships with cyber safeguards on by default. A retuned tokenizer counts ~1.0-1.35x more tokens per task. Intro $2/$10 through Aug 31 2026, then $3/$15. Landed the same day Fable 5 and Mythos 5 came back online.
models.pricing: $2 in / $10 out per 1M intro (through Aug 31 2026), then $3/$15

models.name: LongCat-2.0
models.notable: Meituan's 1.6T sparse-MoE agentic coding flagship, open-sourced under MIT — and the largest model China claims to have trained END-TO-END on ~50,000 domestic Chinese ASICs, with none of the US-restricted hardware. Revealed as 'Owl Alpha,' the stealth model that spent two months topping OpenRouter. SWE-bench Pro 59.5 edges GPT-5.5 (58.6); Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.8, SWE-bench Multilingual 77.3. Native 1M context, ~48B avg active params. Caveat: weights were 'coming soon' at announcement (GitHub/HF placeholders), so it's open-in-intent but not yet downloadable.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, audio, video in; text out)
models.notable: Fast, cheap Flash-tier model that beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on several agentic/coding benchmarks while running ~3x faster; 1M context, natively multimodal, GA across the Gemini app, AI Studio and Gemini API.

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.notable: xAI's 'cheap frontier' flagship (the lab now branded SpaceXAI after the SpaceX tie-up and the ~$60B Cursor acquisition), co-trained with the Cursor coding editor. Musk calls it 'Opus-class but faster, more token-efficient and lower cost.' UPDATE (Aug 8): under Artificial Analysis's v4.1.1 patch the high-effort tier re-scores to 56 from 54, seventh overall behind Claude Opus 5 (63), Claude Fable 5 (62), GPT-5.6 Sol (61), Kimi K3 (60), Qwen3.8-Max (58) and the 57s (Muse Spark 1.2, GPT-5.6 Terra). Standout token efficiency: ~16K output tokens per SWE-bench Pro task vs ~67K for Opus 4.8 (4.2x fewer); ~1.9M avg tokens/task vs Fable 5's 7.2M in Claude Code. Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.3%, SWE-bench Pro 64.7, GDPval-AA #4 (Elo 1543). Default in Grok Build, ~80 tok/s. Context cut to 500K from Grok 4.3's 1M. $2/$6. x.ai's model docs still top out at grok-4.5 -- no grok-4.6 endpoint has appeared.

models.name: Tencent Hy3
models.notable: Open-weight (Apache 2.0) 295B/21B-active MoE; final GA of the Hunyuan 3 line, positioned to rival GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4 at smaller size.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.notable: The balanced middle tier of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family. Shipped alongside Sol and Luna in the Jun 26 gov-gated preview; went broadly public Jul 9 2026 across API, ChatGPT and Codex after the Commerce Dept (CAISI) cleared the safety hold. Carries its own independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score: 55 (v4.1, max effort) — tying GPT-5.5 and sitting one tier below Sol (59). PRICE CUT (Jul 30 2026): OpenAI dropped Terra roughly 20% to $2 in / $12 out per million tokens, down from $2.50 / $15, about three weeks after the public launch. OpenAI credits efficiency gains found while building GPT-5.6 — including the model rewriting and optimizing its own production inference code — rather than any change to the weights.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.notable: The fastest, cheapest tier of the GPT-5.6 family, aimed at high-volume low-latency work. Went broadly public Jul 9 2026 with Sol and Terra after the government access-review hold lifted. Carries its own independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score: 51 (v4.1, max effort) - the entry point of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 lineup behind Terra (55) and Sol (59). PRICE CUT (Jul 30 2026): OpenAI cut Luna by 80% to $0.20 in / $1.20 out per million tokens, down from $1 / $6 - the steepest single price move in the GPT-5.6 line and the deepest discount OpenAI has taken on a current-generation model this year. Same weights, same benchmarks; the reduction is attributed to inference-stack efficiency gains from GPT-5.6's own code optimization work. DEFAULT MODEL (Aug 6 2026): OpenAI made Luna the default model for every ChatGPT user, free and paid, replacing GPT-5.5 Instant; OpenAI says responses containing at least one factual error are 62% less common with Luna than with the model it replaces.

models.name: GPT-Live-1
models.modality: audio+text in, audio+text out (full-duplex real-time voice)
models.notable: OpenAI's first full-duplex voice model — it keeps processing incoming audio while it speaks, so users can interrupt, pause to think, or hear natural backchannels ('mhmm', 'yeah') without it cutting out. Decouples the voice layer from reasoning: it handles simple turns itself and delegates web search / harder queries to GPT-5.5 running asynchronously in the background, talking to the user while that computation happens. Ships with a lighter GPT-Live-1 mini tier; GPT-Live-1 is the default voice for Go/Plus/Pro users, mini for Free, rolling out globally on iOS, Android and web from Jul 8 2026. OpenAI reports GPQA 84.2% at its highest reasoning setting (up from Advanced Voice Mode's 45.3%). API access for developers is planned but not yet priced.

models.name: Meta Muse Spark 1.1
models.notable: Meta's FIRST paid model — a pivot from the free-at-meta.ai original Muse Spark to charging on the new Meta Model API ($1.25 in / $4.25 out, $20 free credits to start). Multimodal reasoning built for agentic work: trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems for low end-to-end latency, zero-shot generalizes to new tools/MCP servers/skills, and actively compacts its 1M-token context. Meta's OWN reported numbers lead on tool-use benches (MCP Atlas 88.1, JobBench 54.7, HLE 62.1 — all above Opus 4.8/GPT-5.5 on Meta's card) but trail on pure coding (SWE-bench Pro 61.5 vs Opus 4.8's 69.2) and multimodal (BabyVision 76.3). Available in the Meta AI app's 'Thinking' mode; closed weights, US-only developer preview. No independent Artificial Analysis Index score yet.

models.name: Inkling
models.params: 975B total / 41B active (MoE, 256 routed experts, 6 active + 2 shared)
models.modality: natively multimodal (text, image, audio, video in; text out)
models.notable: The FIRST model from Thinking Machines Lab, the startup founded by ex-OpenAI CTO Mira Murati (record $2B seed at $12B post). Open-weight 975B/41B-active MoE with a 1M-token context, pretrained on 45T tokens and post-trained with 30M+ RL rollouts; encoder-free multimodal (images as 40x40 patches, audio as discrete dMel spectrograms), with 'controllable thinking effort.' UPDATE (Jul 17): Artificial Analysis published its first independent score — 41 on the AA Intelligence Index (v4.1) — the bottom of the ten-model >40 cluster and a notch below the closed frontier, confirming Thinking Machines' pitch of leading token efficiency rather than raw ceiling (vendor: GPQA 87.2, AIME 2026 97.1, SWE-bench Verified 77.6, HLE-with-tools 46.0). A preview Inkling-Small (276B/12B active) shipped alongside; full weights on Hugging Face, live for fine-tuning on the company's Tinker platform.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.notable: Shanghai lab MiniMax's open-weight flagship — pitched as the first single open model to combine frontier-level coding, a 1M-token context and native multimodality in one MoE (428B total / 23B active). Very cheap at $0.30/$1.20 per 1M. Vendor-reported SWE-bench Pro ~59.0%. Announced Jun 1, live on Hugging Face by Jun 7, and featured among the 261 large models debuting at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai (Jul 17-20). Backfilled here as a real, confirmed open model that was missing from the tracker.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.params: 2.8T total (sparse MoE, 16 of 896 experts active per token)
models.notable: Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts flagship, billed as the world's first 'open 3T-class' model — 16 of 896 experts active per token (104B active), native vision via MoonViT-V2, 1M context, built on two new attention tricks (Kimi Delta Attention + Attention Residuals). Artificial Analysis scored it 57 on the AA Intelligence Index v4.1, ranked #4/189, between GPT-5.6 Sol (59) and Claude Opus 4.8 (56) — the strongest open-lineage model measured so far. WEIGHTS SHIPPED (Jul 27 2026): the open-weight drop landed on schedule on Hugging Face — 96 shards, roughly 1.56 TB in MXFP4 weights with MXFP8 activations, making it the largest open-weight model ever released. The license is NOT the Modified MIT that was widely expected: it is a custom 'Kimi K3 License' that permits free use but requires a commercial agreement for large service providers. Moonshot also open-sourced its attention kernels and MoE library, and recommends vLLM, SGLang or TokenSpeed for inference. Practical caveat: at ~1.56 TB, almost nobody can self-host it. Vendor-reported figures (GPQA Diamond 93.5, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3, BrowseComp 91.2, HLE-Full 43.5) beat Opus 4.8/GPT-5.5 on Moonshot's own suite while trailing Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.notable: Google's new workhorse Flash tier, shipped Jul 21 alongside 3.5 Flash-Lite and a gov-only 3.5 Flash Cyber. Builds on 3.5 Flash: uses ~17% fewer output tokens on the Artificial Analysis Index with fewer reasoning steps/tool calls, and its knowledge cutoff finally advances from Jan 2025 to Mar 2026. Reported gains vs 3.5 Flash include OSWorld-Verified 83.0% (from 78.4), MLE-bench 63.9% (from 49.7), and GDPval-AA v2 1421 (from 1349). Priced at $1.50/$7.50 per 1M (output down from 3.5 Flash's $9). CONFIRMED Jul 31 2026: Artificial Analysis now scores it 50 on the Intelligence Index, tying DeepSeek's V4-Flash-0731 - though DeepSeek reaches that number at roughly a tenth of the price. Google confirmed on launch day that its flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro is still in partner testing (a fourth missed target) and that Gemini 4 pre-training has begun.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.notable: Google's cheapest, fastest model in the 3.5 family, built for high-throughput/low-latency work like agentic search and document processing, with built-in computer use. ~350 output tokens/sec. Big jumps over the Mar 2026 3.1 Flash-Lite: Terminal-Bench 2.1 54% (from 31), SWE-bench Pro 54.2% (from 49.6), OSWorld-Verified 74.0% (from 65.1), GDM-MRCR v2 72.2%. Aggressively priced at $0.30/$2.50 per 1M.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
models.notable: A security-tuned model built on top of 3.5 Flash and fine-tuned to find and fix software vulnerabilities, delivered through Google DeepMind's CodeMender agent. Initially available only to governments and trusted partners as a limited-access pilot — Google's answer to the specialized cyber-defense tier (cf. OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, Anthropic's Mythos 5). No public benchmarks or pricing at launch.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.notable: New frontier flagship succeeding Opus 4.8; adds a user-set low/medium/high effort control, keeps flat $5/$25 pricing and a 1M-token context. UPDATE (Aug 8): Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v4.1.1 patch - graders upgraded to GPT-5.6 Luna (medium) and the tau-cubed-Banking eval moved to upstream v1.0.1 - re-scored the model at 63 at max and xhigh effort, up from 61, and it stays sole #1 on the leaderboard; the high-effort tier now reads 61 and medium 59. Claude Fable 5 (with fallback) sits second at 62, GPT-5.6 Sol (max) at 61, Kimi K3 (max) at 60 and Qwen3.8-Max at 58. It jointly leads AA's Coding Agent Index, hits 89% on Terminal-Bench v2.1, scores 79.2 on SWE-bench Pro, and posts 1861 Elo on GDPval-AA v2 and 1720 on AA-Briefcase. Cost per Intelligence Index task is $2.03 vs $2.75 for Fable 5 - the cheapest frontier-tier intelligence measured. Weak spot: factual knowledge, with a ~50% hallucination rate. Very verbose. DISTRIBUTION: live on the Anthropic API, Claude.ai, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry and GitHub Copilot; a 'Fast mode' runs at roughly 2.5x speed for $10 in / $50 out.

models.name: Fugu-Cyber
models.notable: Sakana AI's cybersecurity endpoint on its Fugu orchestrator — described as a multi-agent system that behaves like a single model rather than a single set of weights. Closed, API-only at sakana.ai/fugu, gated behind an application review with a stated use case and verified contact; billed on Sakana's Token Plan with rates unpublished. Self-reported CyberGym 86.9% and CTI-REALM 72.1%, which Sakana calls comparable to GPT-5.5-Cyber and Claude Mythos 5 Preview. Parameters, context window and modality are all undisclosed, and Sakana published neither the benchmark methodology nor the agent configurations behind those scores — treat both numbers as vendor-claimed and unreplicated.

models.name: Meta Muse Image
models.notable: The model Meta developed internally under the codename 'Mango'; shipped free inside the Meta AI app, Instagram Stories and WhatsApp, and drew immediate user pushback over training on people's own photos.

models.name: FLUX 3
models.modality: text/image in; image, video with synchronized audio, and robot action out
models.notable: Black Forest Labs' first move off pure image generation into a unified multimodal frontier model: one set of weights, built on a 'Self-Flow' approach that aligns multimodal generation and understanding in the same architecture, generating image, video with native synchronized audio (dialogue, SFX and score produced in the same inference pass rather than stitched), and robot action prediction. FLUX 3 Video reached general availability on Aug 4 2026 via the BFL API and select partners, twelve days after the family's launch -- clips up to 20 seconds with audio generated alongside the frames, HD (720p) native with FHD supported, and three request modes (text-to-video, image-to-video with keyframes, and video continuation) sharing a single flux-3-video endpoint. Published pricing is per-second and includes audio: $0.06/sec HD draft, $0.17/sec HD standard, $0.29/sec FHD standard, with video continuation roughly double. FLUX 3 Action remains partner-gated (Canva, Burda, Magnific, Krea, Picsart, plus mimic robotics with Audi); FLUX 3 Image and FLUX 3 Dev, the promised open-weight backbone, are both still unreleased with no announced dates. No published benchmarks -- BFL claims only that FLUX 3 Video 'leads in early evaluations against frontier video models.' The FLUX-mimic robotics variant claims fine-tuning to new manipulation tasks on as little as 30 minutes of robot data where prior approaches needed 30+ hours.

models.name: poolside Laguna S 2.1
models.notable: An open-weight agentic-coding model poolside bills as 'the West's most capable open-weight model' — 118B total / 8B active MoE released under the Linux Foundation's OpenMDW-1.1 license on Hugging Face, plus poolside's own API and OpenRouter. The pitch is size-for-capability: it posts 70.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 78.5% on SWE-bench Multilingual while being small enough to run on a single NVIDIA DGX Spark, which poolside frames as a way to move high-volume agentic work off metered APIs onto owned hardware. Trained end to end in under four weeks on 4,000 H200 GPUs. Vendor-reported numbers; no independent run yet.

models.name: Ling-3.0-flash
models.notable: Ant Group's efficiency play from its inclusionAI lab — a hybrid-reasoning MoE with a thinking/non-thinking toggle, 124B total but only ~5.1B active per token, built on a hybrid-linear attention stack mixing Kimi Delta Attention and Multi-head Latent Attention layers at a 5:1 ratio. 262K native context with 1M stated as the scaling target. Ant claims it matches or beats its own ~1T Ling-2.6 flagship on most benchmarks at 1/8 the total and 1/12 the active parameters, but published no benchmark table or technical report. Announced as Apache 2.0, yet no weights were posted to the inclusionAI Hugging Face org as of Jul 26 — so it is endpoint-only today, free through Aug 3 2026 via OpenRouter (hosted by Novita), Vercel AI Gateway and ZenMux. Surfaced on inference endpoints before Ant announced it.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Max-Preview
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, video, documents in), text out
models.notable: Alibaba's preview of its next flagship, announced Jul 19 at WAIC in Shanghai days after Moonshot's Kimi K3 -- a 2.4T-parameter sparse-MoE multimodal model with a 1M-token context inherited from Qwen3.7-Max, aimed at coding, agentic workflows and long-horizon 'professional cowork' tasks. Ran only as a preview on the Alibaba Cloud Token Plan, Qoder and QoderWork at roughly 10% of standard pricing, with no published benchmarks -- Alibaba claimed only that it was 'second only to Fable 5.' Superseded on Aug 3 2026 by the full Qwen3.8-Max release, which published benchmark numbers, set API pricing at $2/$6 per 1M tokens and committed to open weights.

models.name: MAI-Cyber-1-Flash
models.modality: text in, text out (source-code vulnerability analysis)
models.notable: Microsoft's first in-house model built purely for security work — finding exploitable flaws in large, complex codebases. It anchors Project Perception, an agentic security platform announced Jul 27 that enters public preview Aug 3 and coordinates three agent pools: red-team agents that hunt attack paths, blue-team agents that triage which risks matter, and green-team agents that write fixes. Microsoft reports 96% on CyberGym when MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is paired with GPT-5.4 inside MDASH, its internal vulnerability-research harness — ahead of Claude Mythos 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol at roughly half the compute, and well above Sakana's Fugu-Cyber (86.9%). MDASH came out of FORGE (Frontier Offensive Research & Generative Exploration), a new Microsoft group led by Georgia Tech's Taesoo Kim and staffed partly by Team Atlanta, winners of DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge. All figures are vendor-reported; no independent replication exists, and neither parameters, context window nor pricing were disclosed.

models.name: Celeris-1
models.notable: First model from Celeris AI Labs, a new lab founded by Tom Hamer and Jesse Clark (previously Marqo) on the thesis that latency is a research problem, not an engineering one. Celeris-1 abandons autoregressive token-by-token decoding for a diffusion architecture: it drafts the whole response at once, then refines it over a few parallel passes. Reported throughput is 1,664 tokens/sec at a 158ms median first-response latency — roughly 24x faster than GPT-5 and 5x faster than Inception's Mercury 2, at 75.9% MMLU-Pro vs Mercury 2's 63.7%. It is only the second commercially available diffusion-LLM API after Mercury, and is aimed at latency-bound production work: agentic tool orchestration, classification, extraction and real-time voice. Closed weights, OpenAI-compatible API at celeris.ai; parameters, context window and pricing were not published, and no independent evaluation exists yet.

models.name: Fugu-Ultra v1.1
models.params: n/a (multi-agent orchestrator over a pool of third-party frontier models)
models.notable: A refresh of Sakana's quality-first Fugu orchestrator rather than a new set of weights — the architecture, API and pricing are unchanged and the only substantive change is swapping newer frontier models into the underlying agent pool, which Sakana says takes about two weeks of training and evaluation per addition. Sakana claims up to +7.9 benchmark points over v1.0, concentrated on ProgramBench and Terminal-Bench 2.1, and says the router now beats Claude Fable 5 across most benchmarks despite not carrying Fable 5 in its pool. Adds a Claude Code-compatible endpoint for terminal use; the old fugu-ultra-20260615 ID is now formalized as fugu-ultra-v1.0. Pricing stays $5 in / $30 out per 1M tokens. Every number is Sakana's own with no independent verification, and the service is still unavailable in the EU/EEA.

models.name: MAI-Image-2.5-Pro
models.notable: Microsoft AI's highest-fidelity in-house image model, in public preview on Microsoft Foundry alongside MAI-Voice-2-Flash. The pitch is accurate in-image text rendering and reliable natural-language image editing, and the strategic point is vertical integration: Microsoft says its MAI models already power Bing, PowerPoint, OneDrive and Dynamics 365, cutting its reliance on OpenAI for first-party features. Priced at $5 per 1M text input tokens, $8 per 1M image input tokens and $106 per 1M image output tokens; Microsoft claims the new in-house models cut costs up to 89% versus comparable OpenAI endpoints. No independent benchmark comparison published.

models.name: MAI-Voice-2-Flash
models.notable: A latency-tuned text-to-speech model in public preview on Microsoft Foundry, aimed at high-volume conversational workloads such as customer-service voice agents. Microsoft says it holds MAI-Voice-2's speech quality while running 2x faster and costing 32% less, priced at $15 per 1M characters. Shipped the same day as MAI-Image-2.5-Pro as part of Microsoft AI's push to run first-party experiences on its own models rather than OpenAI endpoints. No third-party quality or latency evaluation exists yet.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Flash
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, video in), text out
models.notable: The cheap, high-volume tier of Alibaba's Qwen3.7 native vision-language series, reaching OpenRouter and international developers on Jul 27 (vendor snapshot qwen3.7-flash-2026-07-15). 1M-token context, up to 65,536 output tokens, and text/image/video input with text output. Priced at roughly $0.03 per 1M input and $0.13 per 1M output tokens under 32K context, tiering up to $0.20/$0.80 in the 256K-1M band -- among the cheapest 1M-context multimodal endpoints available. Alibaba's own docs claim stronger multimodal grounding, object recognition and spatial reasoning than Qwen3.6-Flash plus more stable agent execution, but publish no benchmark table; no independent evaluation exists yet and weights are not released, unlike the open Qwen3.5 line.

models.name: Gemini Robotics 2
models.modality: vision + language in, robot motor control (and text) out
models.notable: Google DeepMind's July 30 robotics release, shipped as three models built on Gemini: Gemini Robotics 2, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that converts camera and language input directly into motor commands; Gemini Robotics ER 2, an embodied-reasoning VLM that plans multi-step jobs, talks to humans and now coordinates multiple robots; and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2, a compact VLA that runs locally on the robot and adapts to a new robot body from a few hours of data. The headline change is whole-body control -- earlier Gemini Robotics models drove only the upper body, while this generation reasons over legs, torso, arms and fingers under one policy, letting a humanoid walk, crouch and manipulate through a single model. DeepMind reports whole-body manipulation success rates of roughly 46-76% on shelf, table and floor picking with an Apollo humanoid on Inspire hands, and 74-90% on insertion and tool tasks with a Franka dual-arm gripper setup; multi-finger dexterity remains uneven, spanning about 32-92% by task. Access is staged: ER 2 is in Google AI Studio and private preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, while the VLA and on-device models go only to early-access partners through the Trusted Tester program.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
models.notable: The formal build of DeepSeek's V4-Flash API, pushed into public beta Jul 31 2026. Architecture and parameter count are identical to the April preview - this is a re-post-training aimed squarely at agent work, plus native Responses API support and Codex adaptation. The jump is large: Terminal-Bench 2.1 goes 61.8 to 82.7 (past GLM-5.2's 81.0, closing on Claude Opus 4.8's 85.0), DeepSWE 7.3 to 54.4, CyberGym 38.7 to 76.7. Artificial Analysis scores it 50 on the Intelligence Index - level with Gemini 3.6 Flash - at $0.14 in / $0.28 out per 1M ($0.0028 cache hit), roughly 35x cheaper than GPT-5.6 Sol. DeepSeek says the update applies to the V4-Flash API only; the V4-Pro API, app and web builds are unchanged, with an official V4-Pro release said to be coming. Separate open weights for the 0731 build were not announced alongside the API beta.

models.name: K-EXAONE 2.0
models.notable: South Korea's largest open-weight model, published to Hugging Face on Jul 31 under an unrestricted Apache 2.0 license. Hybrid-attention mixture-of-experts with 750B total and roughly 37B active parameters per token -- 78 layers (2 dense, 76 sparse), 256 total experts with 8 activated plus 1 shared expert, 6,144 hidden dimension -- more than triple the size of K-EXAONE 1.0. Context window of 262,144 tokens and support for 10 languages: Korean, English, Spanish, German, Japanese, Vietnamese, French, Italian, Polish and Portuguese. LG reports an average of 70.1 across 24 benchmark evaluations versus 63.3 for version 1.0, with roughly a 30% gain on three coding and agentic-coding benchmarks. The model is LG's submission to the Korean government's National AI Foundation Model project, which funds foundation models built from scratch on domestic technology.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Max
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, video in), text out
models.notable: Alibaba's full flagship release behind July 19's Qwen3.8-Max-Preview, announced Aug 2-3 with published benchmarks for the first time. A 2.4-trillion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts multimodal model taking text, image and video, with a 1M-token context (991K max input, 983K with thinking on, 131K max output). Priced at $2.00 per 1M input and $6.00 per 1M output, with cached input at $0.25 -- roughly a third of frontier-flagship pricing. Artificial Analysis has now run it independently: it scores 58 on the Intelligence Index (v4.1), placing it fourth overall behind Claude Opus 5 (61), Claude Fable 5 (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol (59), and ahead of Kimi K3 (57), Claude Opus 4.8 (56) and every current model from Google, Meta and xAI. The number was volatile: AA first published 53, withdrew it after intermittent endpoint failures, re-ran on Alibaba's public API for 56, and the live page now reads 58. Cost per Intelligence Index run more than doubled versus the prior Qwen Max at roughly $1.14 per task, and the model emitted 150M output tokens over the eval -- verbose relative to peers. Alibaba's own numbers still show Fable 5 ahead on the hard coding suite: SWE-bench Pro 80.0 vs 67.7, DeepSWE 1.1 70.0 vs 56.6 and FrontierSWE 88.8 vs 73.5. Open weights for Qwen3.8-Max and a smaller Qwen3.8-27B remain promised on Hugging Face and ModelScope but have not shipped.

models.name: Inkling-Small
models.modality: natively multimodal (text, image, audio in; text out)
models.notable: Thinking Machines Lab's second open-weights release, shipped roughly two weeks after Inkling and now out of preview with full Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face. A 276B-total / 12B-active mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context and native text, image and audio input, it lands at 40 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.1) -- one point behind the 975B/41B-active Inkling (41) at roughly a quarter the active size, and well above the ~25 median for comparable open models. Trained with an improved pre-training mix, on-policy distillation using Inkling as the teacher, and two extra weeks of agentic-coding RL; it beats its larger sibling on SWE-bench Verified (80.2 vs 77.6) while trailing on HLE (31.6 vs 46.0) and SimpleQA Verified (20.6 vs 43.9). Priced at $0.30 in / $1.20 out per 1M on the company's Tinker platform, serving ~130 output tok/s. Runs on 4x B300 or 8x H200 in BF16 (600GB VRAM), 180GB in NVFP4, and a single B300 at W4A4.

models.name: Meta Muse Spark 1.2
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, video, audio, PDF in; text out)
models.notable: Meta's flagship reasoning model refresh, shipped Aug 5 alongside Muse Code -- Meta's first coding agent -- and explicitly co-trained with it. Muse Code is a terminal agent that installs with a single command, runs parallel sub-agents (implementers plus concurrent reviewers) with git-worktree isolation and a crash-safe event log, and is aimed at long-running background workstreams; it is in beta and the Meta Model API is in public preview, with distribution also via OpenRouter. Muse Spark 1.2 keeps the 1M-token context and takes text, image, video, audio and PDF input. UPDATE (Aug 8): Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v4.1.1 patch has now propagated down the board and the model's xhigh tier reads 57, up from 54 -- Meta's best placing to date, sixth overall, ahead of Grok 4.5 (56) and level with GPT-5.6 Terra (57), six points behind Claude Opus 5 (63). On Meta's own published comparison it is second-best behind Claude Opus 5 on both Terminal-Bench 2.1 (82.9) and DeepSWE 1.1 (59.3); Meta also published Meta Internal Coding Bench and GDPval results as images without a methodology write-up. Pricing is unchanged from Muse Spark 1.1 at $1.25 per 1M input and $4.25 per 1M output, with cached input at $0.15 and a no-training guarantee; a 'contributor' tier drops that to $0.10/$0.20 in exchange for letting Meta train on prompts and completions. Weights are not open.

models.name: Ling-3.0-tiny
models.notable: The small sibling to July's Ling-3.0-flash, and the second model Ant Group's inclusionAI lab has pushed straight onto inference endpoints rather than a model page. A hybrid-reasoning mixture-of-experts with 7.9B total parameters but only ~1.3B active per token, a 256K context and up to 32K output tokens, carrying the same switchable thinking/instant modes as the flash tier plus native function calling and prompt caching. Positioned for responsive agents, instruction following and multi-turn conversation at resource-sensitive deployment sizes. Available via OpenRouter (hosted by Novita) and Vercel AI Gateway, free through Aug 13-14 2026; after that it falls back to provider pricing with no gateway markup. inclusionAI says weights will be open-sourced but has posted none yet and named no license -- the same pattern that left Ling-3.0-flash endpoint-only for weeks despite an Apache 2.0 announcement. No benchmark table, technical report or independent evaluation exists.

models.name: LFM2.5-2.6B
models.params: 2.69B dense (30 layers: 22 short-convolution + 8 grouped-query attention blocks)
models.notable: Liquid AI's on-device agentic model, announced Aug 4 2026 as 'Deploy Agents Everywhere' and pushed to Hugging Face in two checkpoints (LFM2.5-2.6B-Base for fine-tuning, plus the post-trained agentic build). 2.69B parameters across a hybrid stack of 22 short-convolution blocks and 8 grouped-query attention blocks, a 131,072-token context, and roughly 34T training tokens, trained via knowledge distillation followed by multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning inside real agent harnesses. Runs entirely locally in under 2.5 GB: 220 tokens/sec on an Apple M5 Max, 113 tok/s on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 CPU, and about 30 tok/s on a phone, down to Raspberry Pi-class hardware. Beats Gemma-4-E4B and Qwen3.5-9B on tool use and instruction following despite being up to four times smaller (ToolSandbox 77.83, Multi-IF 80.07, IFStruct 85.49). Released under Liquid's lfm1.0 license; Liquid explicitly does not recommend it for coding or knowledge-heavy work.

models.name: SeedRealtime
models.modality: natively multimodal full-duplex (audio, video, text in; speech and text out)
models.notable: ByteDance Seed's Aug 5 2026 release: a native audio-video full-duplex large model that processes audio, video and text streams continuously while it is still listening, rather than waiting for the user to finish a turn. Instead of chaining separate speech-recognition, vision, language and text-to-speech modules, it uses a unified end-to-end architecture that natively fuses the three streams, deciding moment to moment when to speak, when to stay quiet, and what on-screen object the user means. ByteDance reports roughly 12% better conversational fluency than its predecessors, crediting improved listening and interference suppression - filtering background noise and avoiding self-interruption. Now shipping at consumer scale inside the Doubao and Douyin apps, with automotive integration flagged as a target, marking one of the first large-scale deployments of full-duplex audio-video interaction. No parameter count, context length or benchmark suite has been published.

models.name: FLUX 3 Video
models.modality: text-to-video, image-to-video and video-to-video, with natively generated synchronized audio
models.notable: The video half of Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 family, split out of July's limited early-access launch and made generally available on the BFL API and select partners on Aug 4 2026. Generates clips up to 20 seconds in HD (720p) with Full HD (1080p) available via upscaling, and unlike most video models it produces the audio natively in the same pass -- dialogue, sound effects and ambient noise, with precise lip-sync across English, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Italian, Indonesian, Turkish, Hindi, Punjabi and more. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, keyframe conditioning, continuation of an existing clip, and multiple coherent shots or camera angles inside one generation, plus a cheap draft mode for iteration. BFL's own all-vs-all Elo puts FLUX 3 first in text-to-video at 1135 and ties Seedance 2.0 in image-to-video at 1051, ahead of Gemini Omni Flash and MiniMax H3 -- self-reported, with no independent arena result yet. Pricing is per second of output with audio included: $0.06/s draft HD, $0.17/s full-quality HD and $0.29/s Full HD for text- or image-to-video, rising to $0.12-$0.53/s for video-to-video. Parameter count, architecture and training data are undisclosed, and no open weights have been released for the video model.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image 2.0
models.modality: text and image in, image out
models.notable: xAI's next-generation image model, shipped Aug 7 2026 as the new Quality Mode on grok.com/imagine and in the iOS and Android apps, with API access said to follow. It is xAI's first new model of any kind since Grok 4.5 in July. The pitch is editing as a first-class capability rather than a bolt-on: a magic-wand tool that alters only the region the user points at, segmentation for precise area selection, and background removal that exports a subject with transparency. xAI also claims stronger typography and layout planning so dense, multi-part visuals hold together and small text renders sharp. On the Arena leaderboards as of Aug 7, the faster 'low' variant places second in the world in both categories -- 1439 Elo on Image Edit and 1320 on text-to-image -- trailing OpenAI's gpt-image-2 (1463 and 1380) in each.

models.name: Shieldstral
models.modality: text and image in, calibrated safety scores out
models.notable: Mistral's open-weight multimodal safety classifier, published to Hugging Face on Aug 4 2026 under an unrestricted Apache 2.0 license. Three billion parameters, small enough to run on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU. Rather than emitting fixed category labels, it is policy-adaptive: moderation rules are posed as plain-language yes/no questions at inference time and the model returns calibrated probabilities, so a team can change its policy without retraining. It covers prompt classification, response moderation, refusal detection and toxicity, over text, images and mixed text-image content through one interface. Mistral says it matches or outperforms open guard models up to 7x its size across text safety, refusal detection, policy adaptability and multimodal benchmarks, and claims state-of-the-art multimodal results on held-out evaluation samples.
